correctness.rationale: Known finite-graph theorem for three-color successor-contact CCA equates eventual synchronization with vanishing integer winding on every directed cycle; package reconstructs winding preservation and a height-gradient propagation argument. In line graph L(H), each vertex-star clique avoids rainbow 3-color triangles precisely when it admits a height lift. For tree H the local clique lifts glue without global obstruction, and a rooted tree multiplies conditional choices (2^{d_v}-1), with factor three at root. A unicyclic H adds exactly one independent cycle-winding constraint; fixing first edge color and recording steps delta in {-1,0,1} leads to constant Laurent coefficient of product [(2^{r_v+1}-1)+2^{r_v}(z+z^-1)] times off-cycle degree factors. Independently enumerated direct CCA orbits on six representative graphs agreed with both formulas. Log-concavity/degree balancing gives star minimum and path maximum; subdivision off-cycle gives multiplicative factor three and unchanged probability. No claim for graphs of cycle rank>1.
